goal: Settle the foundations of the git-workflow plugin (the checked GitHub and tool behaviours, the token service and the component declaration) so that the tool image, release core, daily loop, monorepo and retirement phases can be detailed on checked ground.

review_focus.focus: The done check counts report rows; it does not test that a row marked confirmed rests on a run against the sandbox. A claim about the behaviour of an App token must not be confirmed from documentation alone.

The sandbox repository may use settings (repository ruleset against organisation ruleset, plan tier) that differ from the consuming projects, so a confirmed row can fail in production. Each row should name the settings it was run under.
The done check counts rows only. The splitsh-lite linkage and libgit2 rows must be checked against the release binary version the image will pin, not against whichever version is newest.
The note must stay a contract and a decision record. Server code or deployment scripts of the token service would exceed what the concept settled, and no done check catches that.

The declaration must hold a single source for a component's paths (the workspace graph or an explicit list per component), and its single-repository case (one component at the root) must be written out. No done check reads the note for either.

abstract.summary: The plan opens the git-workflow plugin by closing what the milestone m1-foundations asks for: every verify claim of the white paper is checked against GitHub and the real tools, the token service interface, developer authentication, hosting and key custody are settled, and the component declaration is settled. Later phases for the tool image, release core, daily loop, monorepo and retirement are outlined only, one per later milestone of the roadmap.
abstract.outcome: Five notes in the concept's notes directory, one of them recording the sandbox: one with a row per marked line of the white paper for the GitHub App behaviours, one for the tool and ecosystem claims, one for the token service contract with authentication, fallback and hosting, and one for the component declaration with its path resolution and pre-release handling. The milestone gate of m1-foundations can then be read off these notes.
abstract.cost: Five tasks in the detailed phase, one note each: the developer's sandbox registration and four research and settling notes. The five outlined phases cost nothing until they are detailed in an amend.
abstract.risks: Several GitHub behaviours the release rests on are unverified and may be refuted, which would change decided concept decisions (the App as the only bypass actor, the GitHub Release created by the App, --latest=false). T1.1 needs a test GitHub App and a sandbox repository that the developer registers first. The token service has no design yet and every remote write depends on it. The white paper marks 18 lines against the concept's 13 claims; the plan covers all 18 and does not reconcile the concept's count.
abstract.success: Each marked line of the white paper has a row with a result and evidence, each refuted claim names the decision it puts in doubt, and the developer can read the token service contract and the component declaration as settled. The milestone m1-foundations gate can then be called met.

phases.title: Tool image
phases.intent: Define the pinned image with docker compose and a .docker directory, choose docker exec or an ephemeral container per call, and give the modules one library function that builds every tool call (roadmap milestone m2-tool-image).

phases.title: Release core
phases.intent: Build release --dry-run and --apply with the minimum check, the version-file writers, the local README generation, the GitHub Release by the App and promote to the release tag (roadmap milestone m3-release-core).

phases.title: Daily loop and guards
phases.intent: Build start, commit and pr, the aggregate status check, rules-sync with the STAGE switch, the pre-push guard and the adapted workflow-status and branch-cleanup (roadmap milestone m4-daily-loop).

phases.title: Monorepo
phases.intent: Release each component on its own, split components marked split: yes with splitsh-lite, baseline the existing child repositories and apply --latest=false in multi-component repositories (roadmap milestone m5-monorepo).

phases.title: Retire the old approach
phases.intent: Remove the old CI except status-checks.yml, replace the classic protection code, and correct the stale project context wording (roadmap milestone m6-retire-old).

decisions.question: Which phases the plan details
decisions.chosen: P1 is detailed; P2 to P6 are outlined, one per later milestone of the roadmap
decisions.reason: P2 to P6 depend on the checks of P1. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: Where the check reports and design notes are written
decisions.reason: It lies inside the project scope trigger and next to the concept's raw input. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: How the GitHub App behaviours are checked
decisions.chosen: A test GitHub App installed on a sandbox repository that the developer registers before T1.1 starts
decisions.reason: The behaviours cannot be checked by reading documentation alone. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: How the token service authenticates a developer (CONCEPT-git-workflow-plugin D48, left to the plan)
decisions.chosen: An existing gh login checked against organisation membership
decisions.reason: The white paper's recommendation in row Q-G; it needs no new credential on a developer machine. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: What happens when the token service is down
decisions.chosen: Fail closed: no App write happens while the service is down
decisions.reason: Concept decision D30 leaves no human write path, and a manual token would reopen the personal-token problem. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: Format of the component declaration (CONCEPT-git-workflow-plugin D44, left to the plan)
decisions.chosen: One structured file at the repository root with explicit lists for checks and version files, and no kind field
decisions.reason: The white paper's recommendation in row Q-O. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: Whether JS components take their paths from the workspace graph (CONCEPT-git-workflow-plugin D46)
decisions.chosen: Yes: the workspace graph and turbo --affected; other components list paths in the declaration
decisions.reason: The white paper's recommendation in row Q-R. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: How pre-releases are handled (CONCEPT-git-workflow-plugin D47)
decisions.chosen: Settled after T1.2 reports white paper line 390 (the git-cliff pre-release counter); T1.4 writes the answer into its note
decisions.reason: The white paper's row Q-H says verify first, and T1.4 depends on T1.2. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: How the plan's tasks are carried out
decisions.reason: No task is bash or hook code, T1.1 needs the developer's own account, and T1.3 and T1.4 are dialogue. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: Whether T1.3 also settles where the token service runs and who holds the App key
decisions.chosen: Yes: the token service note gets a Service hosting section naming the hosting and the key custody
decisions.reason: The m1 gate says the token service is settled, and concept D6 says the App private key never reaches a developer machine. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: Which task owns the white paper lines 411 and 654
decisions.chosen: T1.1 takes both lines; its report holds eleven rows
decisions.reason: Both are GitHub latest-release behaviour under concept decision D56; the white paper marks 18 lines and no task owned these two. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: How the verify runs prove the notes
decisions.chosen: The verify runs test content: the result column of each row, a named decision on refuted or changed rows of T1.1, the citation of L500 in the token service note and of L390 in the component declaration note, and no TBD, TODO or open question
decisions.reason: A structure-only check passed empty or TBD notes. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: How the sandbox prerequisite of plan decision D3 is enforced
decisions.chosen: A developer-owned task T1.0 writes sandbox.md; T1.1 depends on it
decisions.reason: No task or dependency encoded the order. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: What the P1 gate proves
decisions.chosen: The gate runs the verify.run of every P1 task (T1.0 to T1.4), each in its own subshell, joined with &&
decisions.reason: A test -s over the notes passed one-row notes and could not see a missing line or the sandbox note; the milestone gate m1-foundations needs the coverage and content proofs. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: Where the token service runs (corrects D10, which had the note name the hosting)
decisions.chosen: The platform is not chosen now: the note fixes the requirements the platform must meet (HTTPS endpoint, private key only in the service's secret store, no logging of tokens, rejection of non-members) and the platform is chosen before the release core phase (P3) is detailed
decisions.reason: The developer chose to name the hosting later and gave no infrastructure to name. Consequence: the milestone gate m1-foundations is met for the contract, the authentication, the fallback and the key custody, not for the hosting platform.

decisions.question: Who holds the production App private key
decisions.chosen: The key exists only in the service's secret store, with no backup; an org owner generates it and rotates it by generating a new key and deleting the old one; a lost key is replaced, not recovered
decisions.reason: Fewest copies, least exposure; GitHub lets an org owner generate a new key at any time and keep several keys active. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: The contract between the CLI and the token service
decisions.chosen: The CLI sends the developer's gh login token, the repository and the permission set the command needs; the service checks the login and the organisation membership and returns an installation token narrowed to that repository and permission set, valid for the one hour GitHub fixes; the CLI keeps it in memory, hands it to the tool container as an environment variable by name, never writes it to disk and drops it after the command
decisions.reason: The one-hour lifetime and the narrowing by repository and permissions were measured on 2026-11-03; a membership check works with the developer's repo-scoped login. Developer answer, approved as stated.

decisions.question: How pre-releases are handled in detail (the answer D8 deferred to the result of T1.2)
decisions.chosen: A pre-release has a release commit like a final release, made by `release <component> --pre <channel>`; the version files carry the pre-release version; the CLI composes the first -<channel>.1 from the base version and git-cliff counts the following ones
decisions.reason: git-cliff 2.8.0 has no --pre and cannot start a pre-release line, but increments an existing one (row L390); one mechanism keeps the tag equal to package.json. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: Name and syntax of the component declaration file
decisions.chosen: components.yaml at the repository root, YAML, read on the host with yq
decisions.reason: Matches the white paper's sketch in Appendix B and decision D6 (a structured file at the repository root); the tool image needs no parser. Developer answer, recommended option.
